reports.title: Mia Gibson
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: It appears that great reliance was placed on the fact that was not in pain and had normal observations. Little consideration appears to have been given to the 'second patient' (Mia), whose condition could not be monitored by paramedics. We heard evidence that in fact not all placental abruptions cause the mother significant pain, or concerning observations, but for the baby, it can be akin to a cardiac arrest. This factor appears to have been overlooked in the trust's subsequent investigation
concerns.hazard: lack of monitoring of fetal condition

concerns.quote: No 'open mic' report was put out to see if other crews could make themselves available to attend this emergency
Dispatchers appear to have allowed a situation to arise whereby the only 2 DCAs not attending other jobs were both on compulsory meal breaks and therefore unavailable at the same time
It was suggested that obstetric emergencies such as placental abruption could
No DCA was available to attend this emergency until 30 minutes after the call, and it took a further 12 minutes for a DCA to arrive after that
The time between the 999 call and being handed over to maternity staff was an hour and 15 minutes

reports.title: Mohammed Khan: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: We have received feedback through our networks that since we issued the revised guidance it is helpful and that it has been used to support the delivery of breech babies.
promises.summary: Revised breech birth guidance issued September 2023

concerns.quote: At 18:55 on the 06.09.22 the trust received a 999 call for Mohammed's mother, Mrs Khan, who was 36 weeks pregnant and it was reported the baby (Mohammed) was being born feet first
concerns.hazard: delayed emergency ambulance response to obstetric complication

concerns.quote: WMAS investigation concluded that the national, JRCALC guidelines for the clinical assessment and management of breech birth were not adhered by the paramedics and regional trauma desk as the clinicians did not appreciate that the delivery was delayed and that intervention to aid delivery should be attempted
concerns.hazard: non adherence to JRCALC breech birth guidelines

concerns.quote: it is not mandatory for paramedics to receive specific training on obstetric emergencies, including breech delivery, either in their foundation training/education or as part of continuing professional development
concerns.hazard: lack of mandatory obstetric emergency training for paramedics

concerns.quote: The clinicians who attended Mrs Khan said they would not have felt confident to attempt the techniques advised by JRCALC even if they had realised they were advised
concerns.hazard: lack of confidence in performing breech delivery techniques

concerns.quote: maternity and obstetric care makes up 3 per cent of emergency ambulance responses
concerns.hazard: low priority allocation to obstetric emergencies

concerns.quote: absence of any mandatory training on obstetric emergencies was putting lives at risk
concerns.hazard: absence of mandatory obstetric emergency training

links.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient training for paramedics on managing obstetric emergencies. The earlier report notes a clear training issue, while the later report states the absence of mandatory training puts lives at risk.
links.earlier_quote: This is a clear training issue, and may well apply nationally.
links.later_quote: absence of any mandatory training on obstetric emergencies was putting lives at risk.
